name: Cross-functional hiring and device-delivery controls

attribution.legal_posture: Localized national-CERT defensive guidance cites secondary reporting; actor attribution remains source-dependent.

caveats: Face-to-face checks must be lawful and remain distinct from facial recognition, nationality profiling and biometric matching.
Sparse professional connections, AI use, phone-region mismatch, and remote work are contextual signals; DPRK affiliation requires independent evidence.
ThaiCERT's item is localized secondary guidance; actor-specific claims should be traced to the underlying primary disclosures.

statements: ThaiCERT warns Thai readers about suspected DPRK-linked fraudulent remote engineering and software-development applicants. It summarizes resume/account inconsistencies, newly created email addresses, telephone-region mismatch, deepfake interviews and use of ChatGPT during interviews. Its mitigation section stresses cooperation among security, HR and legal teams; controlled device pickup; scrutiny of delivery addresses; face-to-face interviewing where appropriate; and integration of validated applicant-fraud indicators into screening systems.

sources.support: ThaiCERT localizes defensive guidance for Thai organizations: coordinate HR, security, and legal review; investigate resume, account, phone-region, and interview inconsistencies in combination; control device handoff; scrutinize equipment-delivery addresses; and correlate validated fraud indicators with appropriate privacy controls
sources.locator: ThaiCERT item 253/68 (IT), three-paragraph threat and mitigation summary
